title: Lightweight Stream Contracts: Pragmatic SDK Ergonomics for Tooling & Structured Output (PRD sketch)
content:
Context and motivation:

We have a large body of hosted-API work around streaming partial responses, tool invocation, and typed/structured outputs. Many of the existing proposals focus on comprehensive protocol surfaces (rich frames, resume tokens, extensive prefetch rules). This sketch intentionally trades complexity for pragmatic ergonomics: a minimal, observable stream handshake + small typed frame set that SDKs can expose naturally to application developers (especially for mobile and edge clients).

Goals (what success looks like):
- Developer friction: client teams can implement streaming tool flows with under ~15 lines of application glue using official SDK helpers.
- Robustness: graceful degradation to partial responses / tool proxies under network/backpressure events without data loss or developer-visible corruption.
- Observability: easily attribute per-frame latency, tool calls, and schema validation failures in Console and traces.
- Cost/latency tradeoffs: runtime can safely coalesce incremental frames for throughput while preserving sensible latency SLOs.

Non-goals:
- A complete streaming protocol for every exotic use-case (we would rather iterate from a small surface).
- Replacing the low-level transport (HTTP/2 / websockets / SSE) — we stay agnostic and provide bindings.

High-level proposal (TL;DR):
- Introduce a 4-message minimal handshake for each streaming session: OPEN -> OFFER -> ACK -> DATA*.
  - OPEN: client creates session with metadata (client-hint, preferred schema id, latency-profile).
  - OFFER: server responds with chosen execution profile, estimated tooling plan (e.g., tool X will be invoked), and server-generated session id (sid).
  - ACK: client confirms acceptance; SDKs surface a single accept-or-fallback callback.
  - DATA*: sequence of typed frames: text-chunk, schema-assert, tool-call, tool-result, end, error.
- Typed frames are compact JSON objects with a minimal required set of fields: frame_type, sid, seq, payload (payload is a string or small JSON blob). We keep validation optional at transport layer; SDKs can toggle strict vs permissive modes.

Developer ergonomics (SDK surface):
- Single method for streaming conversations: client.streamConversation(opts) returns a StreamSession object with small event handlers: onPartial, onToolCall(toolMeta), onToolResult(toolMeta, result), onSchemaViolation(err), onComplete().
- Default behavior: when onToolCall occurs, SDK will (a) synchronously emit a toolCall event to application, (b) if application doesn't respond within configurable toolTimeout, SDK will optionally return a best-effort proxy or fallback (server-provided).
- Minimal example (pseudo-code):

const s = client.streamConversation({schema: 'order-v1', latency: 'interactive'});
s.onPartial(text => renderChunk(text));
s.onToolCall(meta => callLocalTool(meta).then(res => s.sendToolResult(res)));

- Structured output helper: sdk.validateFrame(payload, schemaId) returns {ok, errors}. The SDK will optionally auto-retry a small subset of schema-fix suggestions (trim fields, coerce types) when in permissive mode.

Tool calling semantics and safety:
- Tool-call frames include tool_id, args_preview (sanitized), call_id. Tool-result frames reference call_id and may stream incremental results (tool-result-chunk).
- Security: tool args preview must be redacted by default unless client sets explicit toolConsent in OPEN. Server will never execute tools on customer behalf without explicit consent flags.
- Idempotency: call_id is intended for at-least-once delivery semantics; SDKs should deduplicate results by call_id.

Backpressure and offline resilience:
- The handshake includes a client-provided flow_budget_hint (tokens per second, or chunks per second). Server will honor as best-effort and include flow_advice in OFFER.
- When network stalls or client memory is constrained, SDK surfaces onStalled() and onResume(); offers a small local buffer with eviction strategy: drop-slowest-chunks (configurable).

Observability and telemetry contract (Console requirements):
- Each frame emits a trace event: frame_sent, frame_received, schema_validated, tool_call_start, tool_call_end, frame_error. These map to token-cost and latency breakdowns in Console.
- SDKs annotate traces with session_id, client_sdk_version, latency_profile, and a compact frame histogram to enable quick SLO debugging.

Migration and rollout plan (phased):
1) Canary: server implements handshake and typed frames for a small set of GPT-like models; SDKs (JS + Python) implement permissive parsing + telemetry hooks. Expose feature flag hosted:lightstream-canary. (2 weeks)
2) Field trial: enable for 10% of new streaming sessions; collect telemetry on schema violations and tool-call rates. (4 weeks)
3) Gradual rollout with opt-in strict mode for customers that want validation. Partner with developer-relations to produce migration guide and examples. (6 weeks)

Open design questions / tradeoffs to resolve:
- Schema negotiation: should server be allowed to send an alternate schema id in OFFER? (pros: server can downgrade gracefully; cons: client confusion). Proposed: allow but require explicit user opt-in via schemaFallback in OPEN.
- Tool consent UX: is pre-authorization sufficient or do we require runtime consent flow? For now, require consent flag in OPEN + explicit onToolCall callback to app.
- Frame size and batching: what is default max payload? Proposal: 8kB per frame, server-side coalescing allowed but must set coalesced:true in frame meta.
- Error model: partial vs terminal errors. We need a small taxonomy: transient, resource, schema, security. Map these to platform retries and user-visible hints.

Success metrics (initial):
- Developer time to implement streaming tool call flow (target < 1 day using SDK sample).
- Schema-violation rate under permissive parsing < 0.5% after two weeks of rollout.
- Tool-call latency P95 (client-observed) improvements over baseline when using local tool fallback < 200ms.

Implementation notes for engineering:
- Server: add session manager that stores ephemeral sid mapping to execution plan; expose OFFER decisions via trace events. Minimal disk persistence for short-lived sessions (TTL 5 min).
- SDK: expose a single StreamSession abstraction; provide utilities for deduping call_id and validating schema via lightweight wasm-based validator in JS and a compiled validator in Python.
- Ops: add stream-level billing tags so Console can surface per-frame billing and attribute to routes/models.

Checklist (immediate next steps):
- [ ] API sketch: formalize OPEN/OFFER/ACK/data JSON contract and publish as a single-page spec. (owner: Ravi)
- [ ] Implement permissive parser in JS SDK and add telemetry hooks. (owner: Lina)
- [ ] Server side: rudimentary OFFER implementation and session id allocation. (owner: Tomás)
- [ ] Security review for tool preview redaction and consent flow. (owner: Eddie)
- [ ] Write a short developer quickstart showing local tool fallback with the JS SDK. (owner: Maya)

Notes to self / loose ideas:
- Consider a compact binary wire option (CBOR) for highly constrained mobile clients later, but keep JSON for initial rollout.
- We should record a short screen-capture demonstrating a streaming tool fallback; useful for onboarding.
- Watch out for accidental PII in args_preview; default redaction rules should be conservative (remove anything matching email/phone/token patterns).

References / related artifacts:
- HOSTED-842: initial telemetry-first stream experiment
- GH PR #432: early SDK streaming helper stub
- CONF-314159: internal notes on schema negotiation

End of sketch.

(If this read as too opinionated: yes. The intent is to get a minimal working pattern that developer teams can adopt today and that we can iterate on.)
